reference: Hakim, I.A., Donaldson, S.L., Meyendorf, N.G., & Browning, C.E. (2017). Porosity effects on interlaminar fracture behavior in carbon fiber-reinforced polymer composites. Materials Sciences and Applications, 8, 170-187.
data_source: Table 1 (tabulated): serial-sectioning porosity and static mode I G_Ic of the three vacuum levels; the same G_Ic means are stated in Section 3.3.1
porosity_measurement: serial sectioning: void area fraction of three polished layers per sample (Image Pro Plus, 25x), the mean of 15 measurements per vacuum level
notes: Hand lay-up and vacuum bagging at three vacuum levels: high (-686 mmHg, 1.49 % voids), moderate (-330 mmHg, 1.77 %) and poor (0 mmHg, 3.43 %). Static G_Ic means 0.52, 0.44 and 0.45 kJ/m^2 (= N/mm), normalized to the high-vacuum group (0.44/0.52 = 0.8462, 0.45/0.52 = 0.8654). The DCB specimens (1 in wide, 6 in long along the fibres, 60 % fibre weight fraction; no fibre volume fraction is given) carry a non-porous FEP film insert at the mid-plane; the paper does not say whether the static G_Ic is the insert or a precrack value, nor initiation or propagation. n_plies = 8 is read from the Fig. 2(d) caption (the insert placed at the panel mid-plane on top of four layers). The mid-section layers around the insert had a higher porosity area fraction than the specimen average (no values given), so the porosity at the crack plane is above the listed means. The 1.77 % and 3.43 % groups give about the same G_Ic (non-monotonic); the paper attributes scatter to void size, shape and location, fibre bridging and resin content. Table 1 also lists the mode I fatigue onset G_Imax at 10^6 cycles (0.010, 0.006, 0.005 kJ/m^2 from high to poor vacuum), not used here.
